title: Growth and safety of infants with cow’s milk allergy receiving a new hydrolyzed rice protein-based formula
author: Zemrani, Boutaina
materials: Macronutrient and HMO composition of study formulas.

The control formula is a commercially available extensively hydrolyzed whey-based formula (Althéra® HMO, Nestlé Health Science, Vevey, Switzerland) with lactose, containing the same type and amount of HMOs as the Test formula. The protein content of the Control formula is 2.2 g/100 kcal. This formula was selected as a control as eHF are the standard of care for non-breastfed infants with CMA. Furthermore, this formula contains the same HMOs as the test formula.

steps.title: Obtain consent and enroll infants
steps.instruction: Explain the study to parents, obtain written informed consent, and enroll singleton infants ≤ 8 months who are formula‑fed and have physician‑diagnosed or suspected cow’s milk allergy (CMA) according to the defined symptom criteria, while applying all exclusion criteria (e.g., intolerance to eHF or rice protein, chronic disease, lactose intolerance, severe anaphylaxis, WHO z‑score > 2).

steps.title: Randomize infants to study formula
steps.instruction: Randomize each enrolled infant 1:1 to the Test (hydrolyzed rice formula) or Control (extensively hydrolyzed whey formula) using minimization with stratification factors center, sex, and age category (0‑≤ 60 days, 60‑≤ 120 days, 120‑≤ 180 days, > 180 days) via Medidata Rave RTSM; set the second‑best probability parameter to 15 %.

steps.title: Maintain blinding of formula allocation
steps.instruction: Package both formulas identically with unique codes on primary packaging; keep coding records separate to allow emergency unblinding only if a serious adverse event requires knowledge of the product.

steps.title: Provide formula and preparation instructions
steps.instruction: Supply powder formula to parents with written instructions to reconstitute with water using an appropriate container (bottle, cup, bowl) according to age and developmental stage; note that the Test formula contains hydrolyzed rice protein, no lactose, 2’FL and LNnT at 1.5 g/L (2:1 ratio), protein 2.3 g/100 kcal, and arsenic below EU limits, while the Control formula (Althéra® HMO) contains lactose, the same HMOs, and protein 2.2 g/100 kcal; minor taste differences may be present.

steps.title: Administer formula daily for 4 months
steps.instruction: Instruct parents to feed the assigned formula ad libitum each day for 4 months; the daily volume may vary with the infant’s age, weight, and appetite.

steps.title: Schedule and conduct study visits
steps.instruction: Arrange on‑site visits at enrollment (baseline) and at 1, 2, 3, and 4 months post‑enrollment; place a phone call on day 7 after enrollment to check health status and adverse events.

steps.title: Perform anthropometric measurements
steps.instruction: At each visit, measure weight (nearest 10 g) and length (nearest 0.1 cm) twice by two trained persons; at baseline and 4‑month visits, also measure head circumference (nearest 0.1 cm) twice, tibia length (tip medial condyle to tip medial malleolus) three times, and femur length (tip greater trochanter to lowest lateral condyle) three times, all to the nearest 0.1 cm; plot weight, length, and head circumference against WHO Growth Standards.

steps.title: Collect 24‑h dietary recalls
steps.instruction: Obtain a 24‑hour dietary recall from the caregiver at baseline, and again at the 2‑month and 4‑month visits to capture type and quantity of all foods and beverages consumed.

steps.title: Assess gastrointestinal tolerance
steps.instruction: Administer the Infant Gastrointestinal Symptom Questionnaire (IGSQ) at each visit and by phone after the first week of formula use; during the first week, have parents complete a daily GI tolerance questionnaire covering flatulence, vomiting, crying, fussing, and sleep duration.

steps.title: Record stool consistency
steps.instruction: Use the Brussels Infant and Toddler Stool Scale; parents record stool frequency and consistency (watery, loose, formed, hard) for three consecutive days before the 2‑ and 4‑month visits and a one‑day retrospective record at baseline.

steps.title: Evaluate allergy symptom score
steps.instruction: Administer the Cow’s Milk‑related Symptom Score (CoMiSS) at baseline and at each subsequent visit to quantify skin, GI, respiratory, and general CMA manifestations.

steps.title: Assess quality‑of‑life questionnaires
steps.instruction: At baseline and the 4‑month visit, have caregivers complete the Food Allergy Quality of Life Questionnaire‑Parent Form (FAQLQ‑PF), the Food Allergy Self‑Efficacy Scale for Parents (FASE‑P), and the Infant and Toddler Quality of Life Questionnaire‑Short Form (ITQOL‑SF47).

steps.title: Monitor formula compliance
steps.instruction: At each visit, ask standardized questions about daily formula volume, interruptions, and any unauthorized formula or cow‑milk‑containing foods; count remaining and returned cans; define a non‑compliant day as any day with other formula, cow‑milk foods, or complementary feeding before 4 months; consider ≥ 85 % compliance adequate; at study end, collect a simple questionnaire on formula liking and preparation ease.

steps.title: Collect and record adverse events
steps.instruction: Record all adverse events from consent signing until the end of the 4‑month intervention; assess type, severity, seriousness, duration, and relationship to study formula at each visit and phone call using MedDRA terminology; no proactive collection after post‑study formula access, but spontaneous reports are accepted.

steps.title: Offer post‑study formula access
steps.instruction: After the 4‑month feeding period, give parents the option to continue receiving the assigned formula until the child reaches 12 months of age.

steps.title: Enter data and perform monitoring
steps.instruction: Enter source‑document data into electronic case report forms (eCRFs); sponsor conducts blinded data quality monitoring, issues queries as needed, and records all data changes in an audit‑trail file.
